title: Begin with the Outcome
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Choose an event that addresses a real business need and naturally connects to a paid service or useful consultation.

sections.title: Start with the End in Mind

items.title: What Can They Achieve?
items.description: What can someone achieve or understand in this one session, and what help might they want afterwards?

items.title: Avoid Broad Topics
items.description: Broad topics like Everything you need to know about marketing do not attract committed attendees. Be specific about the outcome.

items.title: One Next-Step Offer
items.description: Every event should naturally lead to one paid service or consultation. Design the event content to make that next step obvious.

items.title: Audience
items.description: Who is this specifically for? Be precise about role, industry, and the problem they share.

items.title: Problem
items.description: What pressing issue does your event address? The event must solve something real, not just share information.

items.title: Specific Outcome
items.description: What will attendees be able to do or understand after the session? Make this concrete and measurable.

items.title: Event Title
items.description: A clear, benefit-driven title that tells people exactly what they will get.

items.title: Next-Step Offer
items.description: The natural paid service or consultation that follows from the event content.

items.title: Speaker
items.description: Turn a Great Talk into Three Useful Follow-Ups → speaking strategy conversation.

items.title: Coach
items.description: Make Your First 30-Day Action Plan → introductory coaching session.

items.title: Consultant
items.description: Find the Three Bottlenecks Slowing Your Operations → systems assessment.

items.title: Trainer
items.description: Create Your First Client Onboarding Checklist → training programme enquiry.

items.title: Service Business
items.description: Prevent the Five Most Common [Industry] Mistakes → demonstration or estimate appointment.

keyPoint: An event without a clear outcome and next-step offer is just a meeting. Define what attendees will achieve and what help they might want afterwards before you touch any software. The event content should make the next step feel natural, not forced.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Audience
actionSteps.description: Write down exactly who the event is for. Be specific, not generic.

actionSteps.title: Define the Problem and Outcome
actionSteps.description: Identify the pressing issue and the specific outcome attendees will achieve.

actionSteps.title: Name the Event and Next Step
actionSteps.description: Write a benefit-driven title and define the natural paid service or consultation that follows.

nextLessonTitle: Create the Event and Registration Page

quizzes.question: What should you define before creating any event in software?

options.option_text: The exact software settings and menu paths
The audience, problem, outcome, and next-step offer
The number of speakers and panelists
The color scheme of the registration page

quizzes.explanation: Before touching software, define the audience, problem, specific outcome, event title, and next-step offer. This ensures the event serves a real business need rather than becoming an unfocused information session.

quizzes.question: Why should you avoid broad event topics?

options.option_text: Broad topics require less preparation
Broad topics attract more people
Broad topics do not attract committed attendees who need specific help
Broad topics are easier to promote

quizzes.explanation: Broad topics like Everything you need to know about marketing do not attract committed attendees. Specific, outcome-driven events attract people with real needs who are more likely to take the next step.

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the next-step offer?

options.option_text: To replace the event content entirely
To make the event longer and more comprehensive
To provide a natural path from free event to paid service
To increase the event registration fee

quizzes.explanation: The next-step offer is the natural paid service or consultation that follows from the event content. It should feel like a logical progression, not a sudden sales pitch.

title: Create the Event and Registration Page
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Create a public sign-up route that captures the right people and provides clear event details.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Memberships → Events → + Create Event

items.title: RSVP vs Ticketed
items.description: Select RSVP for free events. For paid events, use Ticketed and confirm payment setup. You cannot switch event type after creation.

items.title: Event Details
items.description: Set event name, start/end, correct time zone, online link or physical address, short joining instructions, and organizer details.

items.title: Headline
items.description: Put the audience outcome in the first headline. Lead with the benefit, not the speaker name.

items.title: Three Takeaways
items.description: List three specific things attendees will learn or achieve.

items.title: Date/Time/Zone
items.description: Show the correct date, time, and time zone prominently. Confusion here causes no-shows.

items.title: Who It Is For
items.description: Help people self-select. If they are not the right audience, they should know before registering.

items.title: Clear CTA
items.description: One clear registration call to action. Reserve my place or Register now work better than Submit.

items.title: Registration Settings
items.description: Review registration deadline, capacity, notifications, and public link.

items.title: Mobile Preview
items.description: Preview desktop and mobile. Most registrations happen on phones.

items.title: Teaching Note
items.description: HighLevel Events automatically provides a registration page. This does not require a separate Sites Form unless you are using an external funnel.

keyPoint: The registration page is a promise. It tells people what they will get, when, and why it matters. A clear page with a strong headline, specific takeaways, and correct time zone will outperform a beautiful but vague page every time.

actionSteps.title: Create the Event
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Memberships → Events and create a new event with correct type, date, time, and time zone.

actionSteps.title: Build the Page
actionSteps.description: Add outcome headline, three takeaways, date/time/zone, audience description, and clear registration CTA.

actionSteps.title: Preview and Publish
actionSteps.description: Check mobile preview, review settings, and publish when ready. Test with a sample registration.

quizzes.question: Where do you start creating a new free RSVP event?

options.option_text: Memberships → Events → + Create Event
Contacts → Import
Automation → Workflows
Sites → Forms

quizzes.explanation: Free RSVP events are created in Memberships → Events. This provides the event framework, registration page, and attendee management all in one place.

quizzes.question: What happens if you choose Ticketed instead of RSVP?

options.option_text: Registration becomes free anyway
You cannot switch event type after creation
You can switch back to RSVP later
The event becomes private automatically

quizzes.explanation: You cannot switch event type after creation. Choose carefully: RSVP for free events, Ticketed for paid events. Test payment behavior if using Ticketed.

quizzes.question: What should the registration page headline lead with?

options.option_text: The audience outcome and benefit
The event date and time
The speaker's name and credentials
The company logo and branding

quizzes.explanation: Lead with the audience outcome and benefit. People register because of what they will get, not because of who is speaking. The headline should answer: What will I be able to do after this event?

title: Send a Confirmation Without Duplicates
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Communicate clearly after sign-up while avoiding duplicate or confusing confirmation messages.

items.title: Built-In vs Workflow
items.description: Either use Events → Settings → Notifications attendee registration confirmation, OR a workflow Event Registration → Send Email. Not both.

items.title: Check Integrations
items.description: Review any other integrations to avoid two emails saying the same thing. Zapier, third-party forms, or other automations may also send confirmations.

items.title: Single Source
items.description: Choose one system as the owner for each message type. Document your choice so the team knows which system handles what.

items.title: Subject Line
items.description: Your place is confirmed: [Workshop Title]

items.title: Event Details
items.description: You are registered for [Title] on [Day, Date] at [Time and Time Zone].

items.title: Join Details
items.description: Actual join link or access instructions. If links are hidden until later, say so clearly.

items.title: Add to Calendar
items.description: Working calendar link if provided. This reduces no-shows significantly.

items.title: What to Expect
items.description: We will cover [outcome 1] and [outcome 2]. See you there!

items.title: Hidden Links
items.description: If your event hides the join link until closer to the session, point registrants to correct access instructions rather than promising a link that does not work yet.

items.title: Test the Confirmation
items.description: Register with a test email and verify exactly one appropriate confirmation arrives with working access details.

items.title: Timing Matters
items.description: Confirm whether online join links appear immediately or at a scheduled time. Set expectations correctly.

keyPoint: One clear confirmation is better than two confusing ones. Choose a single message owner, include all necessary details, and test that exactly one appropriate email arrives with working access information. Duplicate confirmations make your event look unprofessional and reduce trust.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Message Owner
actionSteps.description: Decide whether built-in event notifications or a workflow will send confirmations. Disable the other.

actionSteps.title: Draft the Confirmation
actionSteps.description: Write subject, event details, join instructions, calendar link, and what to expect.

actionSteps.title: Test and Verify
actionSteps.description: Register with a test email. Confirm exactly one confirmation arrives with correct details and working links.

quizzes.question: Why should only one system send the confirmation?

options.option_text: To make the event look more exclusive
Because HighLevel only allows one email system
To prevent duplicate, confusing messages
To save money on email sending

quizzes.explanation: Duplicate confirmations confuse registrants and make your event look unprofessional. Choose one message owner — either built-in notifications or a workflow — and disable the other.

quizzes.question: What should you do if join links are hidden until closer to the event?

options.option_text: Promise the link in the confirmation anyway
Point registrants to correct access instructions and explain when links become available
Send the link via SMS instead
Do not send any confirmation until the link is ready

quizzes.explanation: If join links are hidden until later, explain this clearly in the confirmation. Provide correct access instructions and set expectations about when the link will be available.

quizzes.question: What is the success test for confirmations?

options.option_text: Exactly one appropriate confirmation arrives with working access details
Multiple confirmations ensure the message is seen
The confirmation is sent immediately upon registration
The confirmation looks professional

quizzes.explanation: The success test is that exactly one appropriate confirmation arrives with working access details. Multiple confirmations are a failure, not a success.

title: Build Timed Reminders
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Make reminders useful rather than annoying by using event-relative waits and testing for late sign-ups.

items.title: Event-Relative Waits
items.description: Use Automation → Workflows with Event Registration trigger filtered to your specific event. Add event-relative Wait actions.

items.title: Practical Rhythm
items.description: A practical starting rhythm: 24 hours and 1 hour before the event. Optional: 7-day preview for early registrants.

items.title: Late Sign-Ups
items.description: Test someone who registers after the 24-hour point. They should not receive a reminder for a time that has already passed.

items.title: 24-Hour Reminder
items.description: Hi [First Name], [Title] is tomorrow at [Time + Zone]. Bring one question about [Topic]. Here are your joining details: [Link].

items.title: 1-Hour Reminder
items.description: We start in one hour: [Title]. Here is your access link or instructions: [Link]. Looking forward to seeing you.

items.title: 7-Day Preview (Optional)
items.description: For early registrants: Here is a useful tip about [Topic] to get you ready for [Title] next week.

items.title: Event Rescheduling
items.description: Test what happens if the event is rescheduled. Reminders should reflect the new time.

items.title: Timezone Display
items.description: Verify timezone display in emails matches the event timezone. Confusion here causes no-shows.

items.title: Cancellation Handling
items.description: Test cancellation and re-entry scenarios. Cancelled registrants should not receive reminders.

items.title: SMS Consent
items.description: Send SMS reminders only where consent and messaging requirements are satisfied.

keyPoint: Reminders should help people show up, not annoy them. Event-relative waits ensure reminders arrive at the right time regardless of when someone registered. Test late sign-ups, rescheduling, and timezone handling to prevent embarrassing failures.

actionSteps.title: Create the Workflow
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Automation → Workflows and create a new workflow with Event Registration trigger filtered to your event.

actionSteps.title: Add Reminder Steps
actionSteps.description: Add event-relative waits for 24 hours and 1 hour before the event. Include reminder messages with join details.

actionSteps.title: Test Late Sign-Up
actionSteps.description: Register a test contact after the 24-hour reminder would have fired. Verify they only receive relevant future reminders.

quizzes.question: What trigger should start the reminder workflow?

options.option_text: Event Registration, filtered to the specific event
Form Submitted
Appointment Booked
Contact Created

quizzes.explanation: Use Event Registration trigger filtered to your specific event. This ensures reminders only go to people who registered for this event, not all contacts in your system.

quizzes.question: What is a practical starting rhythm for event reminders?

options.option_text: One reminder immediately after registration
Every hour for 24 hours before the event
24 hours and 1 hour before the event
Only after the event has ended

quizzes.explanation: A practical starting rhythm is 24 hours and 1 hour before the event. This gives people time to prepare without overwhelming them. Test late sign-ups to ensure reminders work correctly.

quizzes.question: Why should you test late sign-ups?

options.option_text: Testing is only needed for early registrants
Late sign-ups are more valuable than early ones
To ensure they do not receive reminders for times that have already passed
Late sign-ups always cause technical errors

quizzes.explanation: Someone who registers 2 hours before the event should not receive a 24-hour reminder. Test late sign-ups to ensure your event-relative waits handle all timing scenarios correctly.

title: Connect Registration to the CRM
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Know who signed up and prevent crossed event journeys by using event-specific tags and proper workflow filtering.

items.title: Workflow A: Registration
items.description: Event Registration (filtered to one event) → Apply M23-Registered tag → confirmation if required → event-relative reminders → wait until after event → If/Else based on attendance → relevant follow-up.

items.title: Workflow B: Check-In
items.description: Event Checked In (filtered to same event) → Apply M23-Attended tag. Suitable for in-person sessions where check-in captures attendance.

items.title: Event-Specific Tags
items.description: For repeat events, use event-specific tags like WS-2026-11-Attended. Next month's attendance should not misroute this month's contacts.

items.title: Registered Tag
items.description: M23-Registered or event-specific equivalent. Applied when someone registers.

items.title: Attended Tag
items.description: M23-Attended or event-specific equivalent. Applied when someone checks in or verified attendance is recorded.

items.title: Remove Old Tags
items.description: Remove prior instance tags or use unique event IDs when duplicating workflows. Old tags cause misrouting.

items.title: Funnel Form Integration
items.description: If a funnel form feeds a Register for RSVP Event workflow action, separately verify whether that workflow-created registration triggers the Event Registration workflow.

items.title: Test Contact Journey
items.description: Create one test contact and verify they reach intended actions only once. No duplicates, no missed steps.

items.title: Do Not Assume
items.description: Do not assume behavior without testing. Platform behavior can vary based on account settings and feature releases.

keyPoint: Event-specific tags are the backbone of proper follow-up. Without them, repeat events create chaos. A contact tagged WS-2026-11-Attended will not be confused with WS-2026-12-Attended. Tag carefully, test thoroughly, and never assume platform behavior without verification.

actionSteps.title: Create Event-Specific Tags
actionSteps.description: Create tags for registered and attended states. Use event-specific naming for repeat events.

actionSteps.title: Build Registration Workflow
actionSteps.description: Create Workflow A with Event Registration trigger, tag application, reminders, and post-event branching.

actionSteps.title: Build Check-In Workflow
actionSteps.description: Create Workflow B with Event Checked In trigger and attended tag application.

actionSteps.title: Test the Journey
actionSteps.description: Create a test contact, register them, and verify they reach intended actions exactly once.

quizzes.question: Why should you use event-specific tags for repeat events?

options.option_text: To prevent next month's attendance from misrouting this month's contacts
HighLevel requires event-specific tags by default
Event-specific tags look more professional
Generic tags work fine for all events

quizzes.explanation: Event-specific tags like WS-2026-11-Attended prevent misrouting. If you reuse a generic Attended tag, next month's attendees could trigger this month's follow-up workflows incorrectly.

quizzes.question: What trigger should apply the attended tag for in-person events?

options.option_text: Event Registration
Form Submitted
Contact Created
Event Checked In

quizzes.explanation: Event Checked In is the appropriate trigger for in-person attendance. This fires when someone is checked in at the event, distinguishing actual attendees from mere registrants.

quizzes.question: What should you do when duplicating workflows for repeat events?

options.option_text: Assume all references update automatically
Keep the same tags and filters to save time
Update tag names, event filters, and verify all references manually
Delete the old workflow before duplicating

quizzes.explanation: Never assume cloned workflows update every reference automatically. Manually update tag names, event filters, and all references to ensure the new workflow targets the correct event.

title: Record Real Attendance
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Distinguish a registration from a verified attendee and apply the correct tags before follow-up runs.

items.title: Check-In Process
items.description: Under the event's Check-in area, use the provided check-in process. Confirm the Event Checked In workflow fires when someone is checked in.

items.title: Manual Check-In
items.description: Have staff or volunteers check in attendees as they arrive. This can be done via mobile app or printed list.

items.title: Test the Trigger
items.description: Verify that checking in a test contact fires the Event Checked In workflow and applies the attended tag.

items.title: Registration Is Not Attendance
items.description: Do not assume RSVP registration means a person attended. Many people register but do not join.

items.title: Platform Reports
items.description: Check Zoom or meeting-platform attendance reports. Verify who actually participated and for how long.

items.title: Manual Tagging
items.description: Apply the event-specific attended tag manually based on platform reports, or use a tested integration that marks real attendance.

items.title: Webinar Funnel Analytics
items.description: Webinar Funnel analytics may show attendance, but transfer of that attendance into contact tags/workflows must be checked for your setup.

items.title: Wait for Data
items.description: Hold post-event branching until attendance reports are available. Avoid telling a real attendee Sorry we missed you because data arrived late.

items.title: Sufficient Delay
items.description: For manually tagged lists, launch follow-up only after review. Set and test a sufficient delay so tagging finishes before contacts reach the branch.

items.title: Verified Participants Only
items.description: The attended segment should contain only verified participants. When in doubt, leave someone in the no-show segment rather than risk a false positive.

keyPoint: Registration is an intention, not attendance evidence. A person who registers but does not attend should not receive attendee follow-up. Verify attendance through check-in or platform reports before applying attended tags. False positives damage trust more than false negatives.

actionSteps.title: Choose Tracking Method
actionSteps.description: For in-person: check-in process. For online: platform attendance reports. Document your choice.

actionSteps.title: Test the Process
actionSteps.description: Run a test event or rehearsal. Verify check-in or attendance reporting works and triggers the correct workflow.

actionSteps.title: Set Review Time
actionSteps.description: Schedule time after the event to review attendance data before launching follow-up workflows.

nextLessonTitle: Follow Up with the Right Message

quizzes.question: Does registration prove that someone attended?

options.option_text: Yes, if they clicked the calendar link
Only for paid events
No, registration is an intention, not attendance evidence
Yes, registration is sufficient evidence of attendance

quizzes.explanation: Registration is an intention, not proof of attendance. Many people register but do not join. Always verify attendance through check-in or platform reports before applying attended tags.

quizzes.question: What should you do before launching post-event follow-up?

options.option_text: Launch immediately after the event ends
Wait until attendance reports are available and reviewed
Send the same message to everyone regardless of attendance
Assume everyone who registered attended

quizzes.explanation: Hold post-event branching until attendance reports are available. Telling a real attendee Sorry we missed you because data arrived late is embarrassing and damages trust.

quizzes.question: How should you handle online attendance for webinars?

options.option_text: Only track attendance for in-person events
Assume all registrants attended
Use the registration time as attendance proof
Check platform attendance reports and apply tags manually or via tested integration

quizzes.explanation: For online events, check Zoom or meeting-platform attendance reports. Verify who actually participated, then apply the attended tag manually or through a tested integration.

title: Follow Up with the Right Message
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Turn an event into useful next steps by sending different, appropriate messages to attendees and no-shows.

items.title: Thank and Resource
items.description: Thank you for coming. Here are your notes/resources. Provide something useful they can act on immediately.

items.title: Booking CTA
items.description: If you would like help putting this into practice, you can book a short assessment/discovery/demo call: [Booking Link].

items.title: Keep It Relevant
items.description: Connect the booking offer to the event content. The call should feel like a natural continuation, not a random upsell.

items.title: Acknowledge Gracefully
items.description: Sorry we missed you. No guilt, no pressure. Life happens and people appreciate understanding.

items.title: Replay or Next Date
items.description: Here is the replay or next session date: [Link]. Give them another chance to engage without requiring a call.

items.title: Optional Booking
items.description: If a quick conversation would help, you can choose a time here: [Booking Link]. Keep it optional, not demanding.

items.title: If/Else Condition
items.description: Add If/Else → Has [Event-Specific Attended Tag]. Use the yes path for attendee content and no path for no-show content.

items.title: Timing
items.description: For manually tracked online attendance, keep the follow-up branch paused until verified attendance tags are applied. Set a sufficient delay.

items.title: Exclusive Branches
items.description: Confirm each branch is exclusive. A contact should not receive both attended and no-show messages.

items.title: Cancellation Handling
items.description: Handle cancellation and refund statuses where applicable. Cancelled registrants should not receive either follow-up.

keyPoint: Attendees and no-shows need different messages. Attendees get thanks, resources, and a relevant next step. No-shows get understanding, a replay or next date, and an optional conversation. Never send the same message to both groups — it feels impersonal and reduces engagement.

actionSteps.title: Draft Both Messages
actionSteps.description: Write the attended message and the no-show message. Ensure they are genuinely different and appropriate.

actionSteps.title: Build the If/Else Branch
actionSteps.description: Add If/Else based on event-specific attended tag. Route to correct message for each path.

actionSteps.title: Test Both Paths
actionSteps.description: Create sample contacts: one with attended tag, one without. Verify each receives the correct message and no cross-contamination.

quizzes.question: What should an attendee follow-up email include?

options.option_text: A demand to book immediately or lose the opportunity
Thanks, useful resources, and a relevant booking link
An apology for taking their time
A request to refer friends who did not attend

quizzes.explanation: Attendees should receive thanks, useful resources they can act on, and a relevant booking link connected to the event content. This feels like a natural next step, not a sales pitch.

quizzes.question: What should a no-show follow-up email include?

options.option_text: A demand to explain why they did not attend
Guilt about missing the event and pressure to book
Understanding, replay or next date, and an optional booking link
Nothing — no-shows are not worth following up

quizzes.explanation: No-shows should receive understanding, a replay or next session date, and an optional booking link. Life happens; gracious follow-up keeps the door open for future engagement.

quizzes.question: How do you ensure contacts do not receive both attended and no-show messages?

options.option_text: Send both messages to everyone to be safe
Manually remove contacts from one list
Only send messages to attendees
Use exclusive If/Else branches based on the attended tag

quizzes.explanation: Use If/Else based on the event-specific attended tag. The yes path sends attendee content; the no path sends no-show content. Confirm branches are exclusive so no contact receives both.

title: Book Conversations, Test, and Reuse
moduleName: Fill a Workshop or Webinar and Follow Up Automatically
learningGoal: Finish the business process by adding a working booking link, testing the complete journey, and creating a reusable system for future events.

items.title: Calendar Link
items.description: Put a real LeadProspectrr Calendars booking URL in the follow-up email. Check the calendar's availability and confirmation settings.

items.title: Test Booking
items.description: Book a test appointment on your phone. Verify confirmation email, calendar entry, and reminder work correctly. Cancel the test afterward.

items.title: Optional Not Required
items.description: Booking is always optional. Some people will want resources without a call. Respect their choice.

items.title: Two Sample Contacts
items.description: Create one with verified attendance, one without. Check full event and post-event journeys in a safe test setup.

items.title: Verify Each Step
items.description: Registration → confirmation → reminders → attendance tagging → correct follow-up → booking link → appointment confirmation.

items.title: No Cross-Contamination
items.description: Ensure attended and no-show contacts receive only their intended messages. No duplicates, no wrong paths.

items.title: Four Key Numbers
items.description: Registrations, actual attendees, replies/qualified conversations, and appointments booked. Also measure opt-outs and delivery problems.

items.title: Duplicate for Next Time
items.description: Duplicate the event and adapt time, joining link, copy, tag names, and event filters. Never assume cloned workflows update every reference automatically.

items.title: Update Everything
items.description: Manually verify all references in duplicated workflows. Tag names, event filters, and calendar links must be updated for the new event.

keyPoint: A system that has not been end-to-end tested is a system that will fail. Create two sample contacts, walk through every step, verify correct messages, book a test appointment, and measure real numbers. Then duplicate, update all references, and run the next event with confidence.

actionSteps.title: Add Booking Link
actionSteps.description: Put a tested calendar booking URL in both attended and no-show follow-up emails.

actionSteps.title: Run End-to-End Test
actionSteps.description: Create two sample contacts. Verify registration, confirmation, reminders, attendance tagging, correct follow-up, and booking all work.

actionSteps.title: Record Metrics
actionSteps.description: Count registrations, attendees, replies, and bookings. Note opt-outs and delivery issues.

actionSteps.title: Prepare for Reuse
actionSteps.description: Duplicate the event, update all references, and verify the new workflow targets the correct event before going live.

quizzes.question: What four numbers should you measure after an event?

options.option_text: Social media likes, shares, comments, and followers
Email opens, click rates, bounce rates, and unsubscribes
Website traffic, page views, time on site, and conversion rate
Registrations, attendees, replies/qualified conversations, and appointments booked

quizzes.explanation: The four key numbers are registrations, actual attendees, replies/qualified conversations, and appointments booked. These measure whether your event system produces actual business outcomes, not just activity.

quizzes.question: What should you do when duplicating an event for reuse?

options.option_text: Delete the old event before duplicating
Manually update time, link, copy, tag names, and event filters
Assume all references update automatically
Keep everything the same and just change the date

quizzes.explanation: Never assume cloned workflows update every reference automatically. Manually verify and update tag names, event filters, calendar links, and all references for the new event.

quizzes.question: How many sample contacts should you create for testing?

options.option_text: None — testing is not necessary for simple events
One is enough for basic testing
Two: one with verified attendance, one without
At least ten to get statistical significance

quizzes.explanation: Create two sample contacts: one with verified attendance and one without. This lets you test both the attended and no-show paths to ensure each receives the correct messages.
